item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 260523
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM EDT Sat Sep 26 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Gonzalo, located just east-northeast of the Cabo Verde
Islands, and on Tropical Storm Fay, located well to the
west-southwest of the Azores.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Evans/Berg

...FAY WEAKENS TO A TROPICAL DEPRESSION ONCE AGAIN...

----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.7N 43.7W
ABOUT 1115 MI...1790 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WSW OR 250 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1009 MB...29.80 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM GMT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Fay was
located near latitude 29.7 North, longitude 43.7 West. The
depression is moving toward the west-southwest near 3 mph (6 km/h).
A turn to the south-southwest is expected to occur, followed by an
increase in forward speed.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast over the next several days.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1009 mb (29.80 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Berg

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 25
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM GMT Sat Sep 26 2026 
951 
WTNT41 KNHC 260841
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  25
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 AM GMT Sat Sep 26 2026
 
As anticipated, Fay's convection is redeveloping early this morning,
even as the storm's overall organization degrades. The latest
subjective Dvorak intensity analysis from TAFB rated Fay at 2.0/30
kt, while objective analysis from UW-CIMSS rated the intensity
between 31 and 38 kt. With the latest scatterometry pass from around
0000 UTC yielding a maximum wind speed of about 24 kt, and
convection still weaker than 24 hours prior, the initial intensity
was set at 30 kt, and Fay has been downgraded to a tropical
depression.
 
Storm motion remains slow, at 250/3 kt. Fay is beginning to turn to
the south-southwest as it enters the southern flank of the
subtropical Atlantic high. Track guidance then generally depicts Fay
being picked up by the prevailing easterlies by early next week.
Confidence in the track forecast has increased over the last several
cycles as models begin to better converge on a solution, but still
exhibit a fair amount of disparity in depicting when Fay will turn
to the west. The latest NHC track forecast has shifted slightly to
the left, reflecting a blend of the previous forecast and HCCA, and
overall suggests a sooner turn to the southwest and then west
compared to the previous advisory.
 
Confidence in Fay's intensity forecast remains low. While the
system remains over favorable SSTs, vertical wind shear and dry
mid-level air suggest an overall hostile environment. Still, Fay's
convection has re-initiated multiple times over the last several
days, just when it appears that the storm is on its last legs. Warm
SSTs may favor this continued, pulsating nature of Fay's
convection, but the current forecast thinking is that the vertical
wind shear currently degrading Fay will make these convective
bursts increasingly difficult to sustain. The latest NHC intensity
forecast keeps Fay below tropical storm strength, however yet
another restrengthening cycle cannot be ruled out. Skilled guidance
seems to favor an overall upward trend in intensity just beyond 24
h, but with Fay currently lacking organization, the latest
intensity forecast keeps the system at relatively steady strength,
before dissipation is expected by the middle of next week.

item.title: Tropical Storm Gonzalo Public Advisory Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026 
000
WTNT32 KNHC 260847
TCPAT2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Gonzalo Advisory Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
800 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026
 
...GONZALO STILL A TROPICAL STORM AS IT MOVES AWAY FROM THE CABO 
VERDE ISLANDS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM CVT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.6N 23.0W
ABOUT 60 MI...100 KM N OF SAL CABO VERDE
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 350 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM CVT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Gonzalo was
located near latitude 17.6 North, longitude 23.0 West. Gonzalo is
moving toward the north near 9 mph (15 km/h). A motion between 
north and north-northwest is expected to continue through the 
weekend, with a deceleration and a turn to the west-northwest 
expected early next week. On the forecast track, the center will 
continue to move away from northeastern portions of the Cabo
Verde Islands today.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Weakening is anticipated, and Gonzalo could become a remnant 
low or dissipate within the next 24 hours.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles (295 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Gonzalo are expected to affect portions
of the Cabo Verde Islands through today before diminishing Sunday.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM CVT.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Gonzalo Forecast Discussion Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026 
000
WTNT42 KNHC 260233
TCDAT2
 
Tropical Storm Gonzalo Discussion Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
200 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026
 
ASCAT-C data valid near 2230 UTC indicated that Gonzalo's
circulation has become poorly defined. At that time, the center of
Gonzalo was severely stretched by about 100 miles from southwest to
northeast. Although the ASCAT did not fully sample the area where
convection associated with Gonzalo is strongest, it did indicate
that the winds have generally decreased since yesterday. Based on
these data and the latest TAFB Dvorak fix, the intensity has been
lowered to 40 kt. It is worth noting that if current trends
continue and the center does not re-form under the convection,
Gonzalo could dissipate later this morning.

Gonzalo still appears to be moving northward, and should continue 
on this track for the next day or so, though the track could jump 
to the northeast temporarily if the center re-forms nearer the deep 
convection. Regardless, models indicate that the remaining 
convection should become disorganized within the next 24 h, which 
would cause the cyclone to become post-tropical. Given the 
environment that Gonzalo is moving into, which will consist of 
increasing shear and cool SSTs, this seems likely. Once it becomes a 
shallow cyclone, the remnants of Gonzalo are expected to meander 
slowly to the north of the Cabo Verde Islands for several days 
before dissipating near the middle of next week.
